rules.label: Essential hypertension
rules.source: AHA, 'How Much Sodium Should I Eat Per Day?' (last reviewed 2025-07-15): no more than 2,300 mg/day, optimal goal no more than 1,500 mg/day for most adults. VERIFIED, but it is general-adult guidance, not hypertension-specific, and it does not apply to people directed otherwise by their healthcare team. https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/eat-smart/sodium/how-much-sodium-should-i-eat-per-day

rules.label: Chronic congestive heart failure
rules.source: UNVERIFIED assumption: about 2,000 mg/day sodium is commonly used in heart failure. No source checked yet; confirm against the ACC/AHA heart failure guideline.

rules.label: Diabetes, prediabetes, metabolic syndrome and diabetic complications
rules.source: NOT FROM A GUIDELINE. The ADA says there is 'no magic number' of carbs per meal and that needs depend on body size, activity and treatment (diabetes.org, carb counting page). 180 g/day (60 g per serving) is this project's own assumption. https://diabetes.org/food-nutrition/understanding-carbs/carb-counting-and-diabetes

rules.label: Hyperlipidemia, hypertriglyceridemia, ischemic heart disease
rules.source: AHA, 'Saturated Fats' (last reviewed 2024-08-23): less than 6% of calories from saturated fat, about 13 g/day or less on 2,000 kcal. VERIFIED, but it is general-population guidance applied to these conditions by assumption. https://www.heart.org/en/healthy-living/healthy-eating/eat-smart/fats/saturated-fats

rules.label: Gout
rules.unsupported_reason: Diet advice for gout is about purine, and the recipe data has no purine column.

rules.label: Chronic kidney disease and end-stage renal disease
rules.unsupported_reason: Kidney diet limits depend on lab values (eGFR, potassium) and need phosphorus, which the recipe data lacks. Out of scope for v1.

rules.label: Obesity
rules.unsupported_reason: No agreed per-serving calorie limit yet; undecided for v1 (see ehr-and-rules-planning.md).
